text:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT STARTED 1793543210 - serving-runtime: rising OOMs on us-east-1 gpu pool :rotating_light:
incidents-bot: Severity: P2, affected: redwood-hosted inference nodes in us-east-1 (g4/g5 pools). Automatic retries causing cascade.

maya-oncall: seeing repeated container restarts on gpu-serve-uk-*/pod-* since ~1793543000. Crash logs show CUDA OOM followed by kernel panic on one node.

alex.sre: copying tail of kube logs, ps output, and dmesg now. quick note: not a single big spike — looks like slow memory creep, KV cache not evicting properly when attention paging triggers.

selena-dev: fyi we pushed a small change to kv cache eviction heuristic last week (rollout 1793000000), might be related.

maya-oncall: next actions: 1) route traffic away from affected node pool (use routing policy: prefer us-west fallback), 2) bump batch limit down on the route (max_tokens_per_request -> 512), 3) force KV cache eviction for model variants serving in pool.

tony-ml: agree. Also add temporary model fallback to smaller quantized variant (q4_0) for premium customers to keep latency SLOs.

alex.sre: commands I'm running:
```
# cordon the problematic nodes
kubectl cordon gpu-serve-uk-01
kubectl drain gpu-serve-uk-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# reduce replica scaling on deployment
kubectl scale deployment/serve-model-x --replicas=2 -n inference
```

maya-oncall: executed cordon/drain on 3 nodes. confirmed rolling evict of pods. evicted pods come back on other nodes but some fail with: "CUDA out of memory: failed to allocate 1.2 GiB"

selena-dev: grabbing a heap profile from a failing pod. attaching gdb/gcore if it survives long enough. patch to force kv eviction: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/evict?model=serve-model-x` exists. running now.

ops-bot: automated mitigation applied: routing-policy updated -> routes using us-east-1-gpu now prefer us-west-1-gpu and dedicated-reserved fallback.

maya-oncall: customer impact: 7% of requests 5xx in last 15m, spike to 12% for a small subset (workspace ids: w-1245, w-9982, w-2031). Noting chat features impacted for those customers.

status-bot: posted incident on status page (INC-2026-045) with minimal details.

alex.sre: diving into kernel logs: dmesg shows repeated "Out of memory: Killed process" entries and then `GPU after reset: ECC errors` on one host. suspect unified memory thrash with attention paging causing host <-> gpu swap.

selena-dev: can we disable attention paging per-model as emergency? I can flip paging_enabled=false on model-config for serve-model-x. Will trade memory for latency but stops thrash.

maya-oncall: do it. Do we have a quick rollback plan?

selena-dev: yes: POST /models/serve-model-x/config {"paging_enabled":false} -> and we can revert. I'll patch for the affected variants only.

selena-dev: patched configs, applied to canary set (10% traffic). Observing canary pods stable for 4m. No OOMs in canary.

tony-ml: good sign. If stable, promote to 100% for that model family. Also prepare to tune kv cache TTLs to avoid fill on long-running chats.

maya-oncall: promoting to 100% now. Updating routing to point customers back.

ops-bot: routing-policy reverted for critical customers.

alex.sre: still seeing a handful of nodes with fragmented allocator memory (paged allocator). These hosts need full restart to recover. I'll rotate them out of rotation and reboot.

maya-oncall: schedule reboot order and annotate maintenance windows. Doing one AZ at a time.

selena-dev: follow-up actions: create a hotfix to force periodic KV eviction when paging transitions occur; add stronger telemetry for avg kv size per-session. Filing PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/serve/pulls/4589

alex.sre: saved stack traces and perf traces to s3://incidents/1793543210/ for postmortem. Collected nvidia-smi snapshots and process GPs.

maya-oncall: customer comms: support to send proactive messages to affected workspaces and offer credits. ticketing updated.

tony-ml: note: we should consider a model-level quantization fallback that triggers automatically on memory pressure. Track as tech-debt/plan.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE 1793544300 - mitigations applied: paging disabled canary -> promoted, node reboots in progress, traffic rerouted. Error rate down to 2.1% overall.

maya-oncall: handing off to alex for next 2 hours for cleanup and postmortem prep. alex, confirm you have the stick.

alex.sre: got it. I'll finalize the list of affected customers, attach logs, and start a timeline doc. Will include: trigger (kv eviction heuristic rollout), symptom (slow memory creep -> OOM), mitigations (paging toggle, node reboots, routing), and follow-ups (hotfix, telemetry, automated fallback).

maya-oncall: adding runbook notes to incident ticket: set `kv_evict_interval=30s` for affected models until PR lands.

selena-dev: will prioritize PR review and test in staging ASAP.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVE CANDIDATE 1793545600 - error rate stable <1%, no new OOMs for 25m on promoted config. Leaving in monitoring for 1h.

maya-oncall: resolving from oncall pov, leaving postmortem owner tag to @alex.sre. thanks all :heart:

alex.sre: starting postmortem draft now.

ops-bot: maintenance note: reboots completed for 3 nodes, 2 nodes still in progress (ETA 15m).

selena-dev: quick note to next oncall: if you see similar gradual OOM pattern, prefer toggling paging off before heavy node reboots — it stops the thrash quicker.

incidents-bot: THREAD CLOSED 1793545610 - final logs archived to s3://incidents/1793543210/ (tar.gz). Postmortem assigned: alex.sre.
